_doc: Coefficients of the per-tile food model (sim/geography/food_capacity.py).

entries.source: Lieth 1975, Modeling the primary productivity of the world (Miami model), coefficients from memory
entries.why: Upper asymptote of the Miami temperature curve.

entries.source: Lieth 1975, Modeling the primary productivity of the world (Miami model), coefficients from memory
entries.why: Miami temperature curve constant.

entries.source: Lieth 1975, Modeling the primary productivity of the world (Miami model), coefficients from memory
entries.why: Miami temperature curve slope.

entries.source: Lieth 1975, Modeling the primary productivity of the world (Miami model), coefficients from memory
entries.why: Miami precipitation curve rate.

entries.unit: g dry matter / m2 / yr per mm
entries.source: Miami model overestimates deserts (Lieth 1975); slope chosen by me to give desert scrub NPP near observed
entries.why: Aridity correction until a water balance with potential evapotranspiration exists.

entries.source: as food_npp_dry_slope
entries.why: Aridity correction offset: below this much rain nothing grows.

entries.source: Miami temperature curve ignores that polar land has no thaw month; ramp chosen so tundra NPP lands near Whittaker and Likens 1975 biome mean
entries.why: Zero production where the warmest month never thaws.

entries.source: Typical energy content of plant dry matter, about 18.4 kJ/g
entries.why: Converts biomass to energy.

entries.source: About 2200 kcal/day for an adult, raised for children, age mix and waste
entries.why: Turns food energy into people supported; a population model with ages replaces it.

entries.source: naming choice
entries.why: Id of the crop source in results and technique factors; every other source id is on its content row.

entries.source: naming choice
entries.why: Which list of the result a content row's species id goes into.

entries.source: Roman Italy 0.6-0.9, medieval England 0.5-0.9, Han North China 1.0-1.5 t/ha (Spurr 1986; Campbell 2000; Bray 1984), from memory
entries.why: Gross grain yield of the best pre-modern unirrigated field before fertility, climate and technique scale it.

entries.source: Growing-degree rule of thumb: little cropping below a few degrees annual mean
entries.why: Share of reference yield the annual mean temperature allows.

entries.source: Dryland farming minimum about 250-400 mm (Mediterranean fallow tradition), from memory
entries.why: Share of reference yield rainfall allows without irrigation.

entries.source: Wheat 3.4, rice 3.6, maize 3.6 kcal/g
entries.why: Energy of grain.

entries.source: Seed ratios of 3-5 to 1 in Roman and medieval agriculture (Columella; Campbell 2000)
entries.why: Kept back for sowing.

entries.source: Post-harvest loss to pests and spoilage, 10-15% in the literature, from memory
entries.why: Lost between field and meal.

entries.unit: fraction of arable land cropped in a year
entries.source: Two-field fallow 0.5, three-field 0.67 (Medieval Europe)
entries.why: Fallow rotation; a technique factor on crops raises it.

entries.unit: km each side of navigable river length
entries.source: Nile valley floodplain about 10-20 km wide between the desert edges; Egypt's cultivated land about 25,000-30,000 km2 along roughly 1,600 km of mapped navigable Nile and delta channels, from memory
entries.why: Land a large river can water, from river length; a floodplain-width layer replaces it.

entries.unit: km each side of non-navigable river length
entries.source: Stream and canal-fed oasis strips are hundreds of metres to a few km wide, from memory
entries.why: Land a small river or stream can water, from its length.

entries.source: Flood-renewed silt matched the best dry-farmed land (Egyptian and Mesopotamian yields, Bowman and Rogan 1999), from memory
entries.why: River-watered land's own soil quality, independent of the surrounding climate class.

entries.unit: fraction of irrigated land cropped in a year
entries.source: Basin irrigation sows every year after the flood with no fallow (Egypt)
entries.why: The flood renews the soil, so irrigated land is not left fallow.

entries.source: Irrigated rice and basin wheat 1.5-3x dryland yields, damped for a mixed pre-modern system
entries.why: Irrigated land is not water-limited and sometimes double-cropped.

entries.unit: g dry matter / m2 / yr per mm
entries.source: Sala et al. 1988 Ecology 69:40, Great Plains herbaceous production vs rain
entries.why: Grass production per mm of rain.

entries.source: Sala et al. 1988
entries.why: Rain absorbed before grass grows.

entries.source: Proper-use factors 25-50% (Holechek rangeland guides), from memory
entries.why: What grazing can take without ruining the range.

entries.source: Forage quality adjustment calibrated to Le Houerou and Hoste 1977 stocking rates, from memory
entries.why: Share of grass livestock can actually use.

entries.source: Seasonal access to dry-season pasture and water, 0.5-0.8, my estimate
entries.why: Pasture not reachable all year.

entries.unit: fraction of body mass dry matter / day
entries.source: FAO/ILCA tropical livestock unit definition, from memory
entries.why: Daily forage need of a grazing animal.

entries.source: Robinson and Redford 1986, rmax = 1.5 W^-0.36
entries.why: Maximum population growth rate by body size.

entries.source: Robinson and Redford 1986
entries.why: Allometric exponent of maximum growth rate.

entries.source: Robinson and Redford 1991 sustainability model
entries.why: Stock at which production peaks.

entries.source: Share of production a pre-modern hunter can find and reach; my estimate
entries.why: Technique factors for hunting raise it.

entries.source: Pauly and Christensen 1995 Nature 374:255
entries.why: Converts primary production carbon to wet mass.

entries.source: Pauly and Christensen 1995; the ten percent rule
entries.why: Energy passed up each trophic level.

entries.source: Typical zone size of the measured shelf_area_km2 layer (cell plus a cell side); used only on maps without it
entries.why: Fishable shelf of a coastal tile.

entries.source: Coastal shelf 150-500 g C/m2/yr, from memory; used until an ocean productivity layer exists
entries.why: Shelf primary production.

entries.source: Measured shelf zones extend far offshore (overlap with neighbours is split separately); pre-industrial craft work the near coast only; my estimate
entries.why: Share of the shelf zone a tiles boats can work.

entries.source: Mean daily temperature of 5 C is the conventional start and end of the thermal growing season (WMO, FAO agro-climatology), from memory
entries.why: Months below it grow no grass.

entries.source: Season of the Great Plains sites behind the rain formula (Sala et al. 1988), estimated from their sine temperature cycle
entries.why: Grass output scales with the growing season relative to this.

entries.source: Cut, dried and stored hay loses much of what was grown to cutting height, weather and spoilage; my estimate
entries.why: Share of stored fodder that reaches an animal in months with no growth.

entries.source: Axe and fire clearance of dense forest was slow and partial before iron tools at scale; my estimate
entries.why: Forest the plough can take; the rest of the forest stays wood.

entries.unit: envelope on metres of mean elevation step between neighbouring cells
entries.source: Plough tillage is limited to gentle slopes (about 10-15 percent); the layer is a coarse 10 arc-minute step so the mapping to local slope is a guess
entries.why: Share of arable land gentle enough to plough; a terracing technique would raise it.

entries.unit: envelope on metres of mean elevation step between neighbouring cells
entries.source: Livestock graze slopes well beyond the plough limit (cattle to about 30 percent, sheep and goats steeper); coarse layer so a guess
entries.why: Share of open land gentle enough to graze.
